title: Recruitment: verify compartment ratios on real measurements
description: Run a bounded, real measurement-table analysis, inspect the current filters and figures, and distinguish host-cell ratios from well summaries and biological conclusions.
objectives: Select a measured project with linked cell, nucleus, pathogen and cytoplasm tables.
Keep the target channel, auxiliary ratios, plate metadata and filters consistent.
Interpret archived overlays, host-cell outputs, well averages and standard-deviation error bars at their correct scope.
Check actual exported identities and calculations rather than accepting a completion message alone.
prerequisite: Use an already measured project and a new working copy. The recording uses four real fields from the archived HeLa siRNA tutorial experiment: 453 cell, 588 nucleus, 998 pathogen and 453 cytoplasm rows. ER channel 1 and the control labels come from recorded metadata, not independent biological validation. Original tables and image arrays remain unchanged. Recruitment has no separate example-download or Live preview control; obtain and validate measurements first.

scenes.narration: Open Recruitment in Home's Assays category. This workflow calculates compartment-intensity ratios from existing measurements; it does not rerun segmentation. Start with a measured project whose cell, nucleus, pathogen and cytoplasm records share valid object identities.

Set Source to a new working copy containing measurements slash measurements dot D B and the merged images. Here we copy four real fields, preserving all selected rows and identities. The source contains four hundred fifty-three cells, not the complete original plate.

Choose channel of interest one, the second plane in zero-based indexing. The archived settings identify this as the E R signal. Check your own acquisition metadata; a plausible ratio cannot establish that you selected the right biological marker.

Set Channel dims to one alone for this example. The current auxiliary ratio columns are overwritten for each listed channel, so a multi-channel list can leave them describing a different signal from the main recruitment column. A single matching channel avoids that ambiguity.

The recorded image-channel mapping is cell one, nucleus zero and pathogen three. These are not the old mask-plane controls, which are no longer present here. Preserve the mapping with the measurements rather than copying these values into a different experiment.

The three group labels map column one to positive control, column two to negative control, and columns three through fourteen to screen. This subset contains only four wells in the first three columns. The labels are recorded experimental annotations, not control identities inferred from the images.

The example uses cell area between thirty-five hundred and one hundred thousand pixels, nucleus area between seven hundred and four thousand, and pathogen area between one hundred and one thousand. Bounds are strict. Pathogen area is summed within each host cell before this last filter; it is not a separate size test for every parasite.

Allow at most one nucleus and ten pathogens per host cell. Child-count limits run before the later area filters. Here the one-nucleus limit removes one hundred three cells from the join; those cells do have nucleus records in the original table, despite the generic console warning suggesting a database gap.

Cell intensity filtering is disabled. For nucleus and pathogen intensity, use minus one and sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six: the GUI retains these explicit bounds, and every used source mean is independently verified within the unsigned sixteen-bit range, so they remove no rows in this example.

Do not tune those bounds by their names alone. With this mapping, the current nucleus intensity filter reads channel three and the pathogen filter reads channel one. The broad demonstrated ranges avoid additional exclusions; they are not a recommendation for selecting positive cells in another dataset.

Cells per well is ten here, but this threshold uses the selected source's cell count before the analysis filters, not the final retained count. The target-intensity minimum also requires the cell's channel-one ninety-fifth percentile to exceed one. These are raw measurement filters, not normalization or statistical significance thresholds.

Keep Plot on. In the current implementation, Plot number zero includes the first enumerated archived image, not necessarily the earliest acquired field; the recruitment charts are generated separately. There is no interactive segmentation preview on this screen. Use Mask or Measure for their own live preview workflows before relying on the measurements.

Press Run and follow the genuine console output. This bounded calculation uses the local measurement tables and does not require an A I provider or a model-training job. Wait for the analysis and figure generation to finish before inspecting the exported results.

Inspect the real archived image and its stored mask overlay. Its label areas differ from the measurement table. Recorded filtering and merging can explain that difference, but we have not reconstructed the exact historical masks. The overlay is context, not proof that an individual displayed boundary produced a particular recruitment ratio.

The compartment-intensity charts summarize retained host cells. Although the labels say by P V, the current reader has already grouped pathogen measurements within each cell. It averages pathogen mean intensities without area weighting; do not interpret these rows as independent parasitophorous vacuoles or pooled-pixel measurements.

The main recruitment value divides the host cell's aggregated pathogen mean by its cytoplasm mean on channel one. Additional panels use percentile, periphery or outside measurements. These ratio axes start at one, so they cannot show all sub-unity values; inspect the numeric exports when assessing depletion or low ratios.

Each well averages its retained cell ratios, rather than dividing well-mean intensities. The chart then averages those well values by condition. Error bars show between-well standard deviation, not confidence intervals. Two positive-control wells can supply a spread estimate, but single negative-control and screen wells cannot. This small, unbalanced demonstration does not establish a treatment effect.

The actual run retains two hundred twenty-three host-cell rows and four well rows. We independently check the exact identities, child aggregates, sixteen ratio columns and well means against the private source tables. A Finished message alone would not prove those joins or calculations correct.

Keep results slash cells dot C S V and wells dot C S V with the saved settings and source provenance. Pathogen area and pathogen count in the well table are means per retained cell, not totals. The slope columns contain constants, not fitted estimates. Review near-zero denominators and nonfinite values before drawing conclusions.

The A I toggle can route a question through a configured assistant. This recording only drafts a question and does not send it or generate an answer. Review provider configuration and privacy before sharing console or image context; an assistant response does not validate the experiment.

In Python, spacr.submodules.analyze_recruitment runs this same analysis from a settings dictionary and returns the cell and well tables. Keep the demonstrated calculation separate from biological validation: verify acquisition channels, segmentation provenance, experimental units and suitable controls before applying it to your own screen.
